title: Characterization of Novel Biomarkers for the Laboratory Diagnosis of Rheumatic Diseases
summary:
In this study, we aim to investigate how measuring CD169 in the blood can help distinguish rheumatic and autoinflammatory diseases from other inflammatory conditions, including acute and chronic infections. At the same time, IL-18 will be evaluated using a novel assay system. We aim to validate the measurement methods, establish reference ranges and diagnostic cut-off values, and analyze potential associations with disease course.

Furthermore, the study aims to better characterize the interactions between immune cells, inflammatory markers, and hormones in the context of immune-mediated diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults aged ≥18 years.

Suspected rheumatic disease with a potential interferon signature (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren’s syndrome, or inflammatory myopathies), based on established diagnostic criteria.

Patients with active or inactive disease to capture different phases of disease activity.

Female control participants without any known acute or chronic disease (e.g., infections, metabolic disorders, autoimmune diseases, injuries, etc.) will serve as the control group.
Exclusion criteria:
Use of non-standardized immunotherapies or high-dose corticosteroids.

Severe comorbidities that may complicate the interpretation of biomarker results (e.g., hematologic or oncologic diseases).
